solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, answers clash); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: D made note of mainland conservationists first

indicators.note: first says the conservationists come before the mainland in the answer

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
NT is the National Trust, a British conservation charity
Asia is the great mainland continent

explanation.surface: Someone records which conservation group got to the mainland first.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the puzzle's theme, Disney: 'D made' points to one of its films. The NT is Britain's National Trust.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantasia is the 1940 animated feature from the Disney studio, set to classical music.

clue.text: D made fellow take partial pathway to religion

indicators.note: partial says only part of the pathway word is used, its last letters cut

parts.note: a road is a pathway
Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A man sets off halfway along a spiritual path.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen is the 2013 Disney animated film about the sisters Elsa and Anna.

clue.text: Disgraced MP would be suffering refusal in Paris through relative

parts.note: non is French for no
per means through or by way of
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A shamed politician is turned away in France, going through a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgraced figure erased from public record, as in Soviet practice, is treated as though they never existed.

clue.text: Phenomena seen over our area

indicators.note: over in the sense of tumbled over, so the letters of our area are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lights in the sky are being reported over the local district.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora borealis and australis are natural light displays, plural phenomena in the sky.

clue.text: Awareness of trendy appearance

parts.note: in means fashionable
sight as in a sight to behold, an appearance

explanation.surface: Knowing what looks fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep understanding or perception of something, a kind of awareness.

clue.text: Exhortation — or warning — to a percussionist?

definitions.text: Exhortation — or warning — to a percussionist?

parts.words: Exhortation — or warning — to a percussionist?
parts.note: a drummer might be urged to strike the drum, or told to clear off

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is both an order to hit the drum and slang for go away.
explanation.definitionFit: Get lost as a warning, or a literal instruction to strike a drum: both readings of the same two words.

clue.text: Disguised one's words when no longer holding firm

indicators.note: holding means the first word keeps the second inside it

parts.note: something that has ended is no longer
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Someone hid their meaning once they stopped standing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like an adjective about resolve; it is the noun, a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting a message into code hides its meaning, so to have encoded is to have disguised a message.

clue.text: According to D, woman goes before March

definitions.text: According to D, woman goes before
definitions.meaning: in the Disney film title Lady and the ..., the lady comes first
to march heavily or hike is to trudge on foot

explanation.surface: In someone's diary the woman's date comes before March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney title pairs a lady with a stray dog of this name, and the word also means to walk wearily.

clue.text: Trivial romance made by D

parts.note: toy as an adjective means small or trifling
a romance is a story, a tale

explanation.surface: A lightweight love tale from someone called D.
explanation.definitionFit: Toy Story is the 1995 Pixar film released by Disney, the first fully computer-animated feature.

clue.text: D's mythical creature was insignificant

definitions.meaning: Disney's mermaid Ariel is the title's small one

explanation.surface: Someone's mythical beast turned out to be unimportant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney title calls its mermaid small, and the word also means trivial or of no account.

clue.text: One has removed foreign body from boy wonder

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and jumbled, so the letters of boy wonder, less those of body, are rearranged

explanation.surface: A surgeon has taken a foreign object out of a gifted child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed ... from' takes the letters B, O, D, Y out of BOYWONDER, leaving WONER, which 'foreign' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is the person who has something: a possessor.

clue.text: Has sir got time to be mad?

definitions.text: Has sir got time to be mad?

indicators.note: got means the first word has acquired the second inside it

parts.note: crazy means mad

explanation.surface: Is the gentleman going mad from serving his sentence?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also reads as the definition: time inside, in prison slang 'stir', sends one mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is slang for prison, and being confined too long makes one crazy, hence the compound.

clue.text: Said "yes" to vivid plant

indicators.note: said means the word for yes is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: aye means yes
bright means vivid

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to a brightly coloured plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild flower, Euphrasia, once used to treat eye complaints.

clue.text: Shortly, stand-in will take books to station

indicators.note: shortly means the stand-in word is cut short

parts.note: a deputy stands in for someone
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A substitute will soon take books to the station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' looks like 'soon' but tells you to cut DEPUTY to DEP.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a station, for buses or trains, or a base for stores.

clue.text: Feature on a group covers page 1

indicators.note: covers means the group word wraps around the page letter

parts.note: a sect is a group

indicators.note: 1 picks the first letter of page

explanation.surface: A feature on a group fills the front page.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspect is a feature or facet of something.

clue.text: The last link in the chain?

definitions.text: The last link in the chain?

parts.words: The last link in the chain?
parts.note: the supply chain ends with the person who finally consumes the product

explanation.walkthrough: Not a physical chain: the chain of supply from maker to buyer.
explanation.definitionFit: The final consumer of a product sits at the very end of the supply chain.

clue.text: Plan girl's trip around boat

indicators.note: around says the girl's name wraps the boat
trip in the sense of a turnover, so the girl's word is read backwards

parts.note: Pam's, a girl's name with its possessive s
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: Plan a girl's voyage round in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' is the reversal signal, as in tripping something over; 'around' then wraps the turned name round the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch map is a rough plan of an area drawn by hand.

clue.text: Admits us equivocally to all grounds, say

indicators.note: equivocally means ambiguously, so the letters of Admits us are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone vaguely lets us into every sports venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadiums are sports grounds, and 'say' marks them as examples of grounds.

clue.text: D made Gladstone confused? Not so

indicators.note: confused tells you to mix up the letters of Gladstone, once 'Not so' has taken away S and O

explanation.surface: Did Disney muddle Gladstone, the Victorian prime minister? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not so' says the letters of SO are left out of the mixed-up GLADSTONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangled is the 2010 Disney animated retelling of the Rapunzel fairy tale.

clue.text: Like D's pride, Marxist finds love in Spain

indicators.note: finds says the Marxist takes in the love letter

parts.note: Lenin was the Marxist Russian revolutionary
love is zero in tennis, written O
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A communist falls in love on a trip to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: D's pride is the lion pride of The Lion King.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, as the lions of Disney's The Lion King are.

clue.text: Would a slow leak be silly?

definitions.meaning: a slow leak lets out drops, so it would be dripping

explanation.definitionFit: Drippy literally describes something letting out drops, and colloquially a feeble or soppy person.

clue.text: More expensive doctor to be exchanged for lecturer

indicators.note: to be exchanged says the two doctor letters, D and R, swap places in the pricier word

parts.note: dearer means more expensive

explanation.surface: A pricier doctor is to be swapped for a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is DR: its two letters D and R trade places within DEARER, turning the opening DEAR into READ.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities a Reader is a senior academic ranking just below professor.

clue.text: Net worth of estate Euripides calculated (without using pi)

indicators.note: calculated suggests the letters of Euripides are worked over into a new order, minus the letters of pi

explanation.surface: The Greek playwright's estate is valued without using the number pi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without using pi' removes P and I from EURIPIDES before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: The residue of an estate is what remains after debts and bequests are paid.

clue.text: Pleasant story following the daft at heart

indicators.note: following puts the story after the middle letters
at heart picks the middle letters of daft

parts.note: a fable is a story

explanation.surface: A nice tale follows the silly at their core.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and easy to talk to, which is pleasant.

clue.text: Look to Spanish uncle to finish carton of cream

parts.note: lo means look
tío is Spanish for uncle

indicators.note: to finish picks the last letter of carton

explanation.surface: Look to your Spanish uncle to use up the last of the cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A lotion is a cream or liquid preparation applied to the skin.

clue.text: D made him say nothing twice

parts.note: to be dumb is to say nothing
twice says nothing is used a second time, as O, the zero-shaped letter

explanation.surface: Disney made him keep quiet, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing' does two jobs: within 'say nothing' and alone as O.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is Disney's 1941 film about the elephant with huge ears.

clue.text: Pessimist has no end of money; that's how he is!

definitions.text: Pessimist has no end of money; that's how he is!

indicators.note: has no says a letter is dropped from the pessimist word

parts.note: a misery is a gloomy, complaining person

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of money

explanation.surface: A gloomy man is skint, and that's why he is gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no end of money' also means has plenty of money, which is how a hoarder is.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards wealth, so he has endless money yet lives like a pauper.

clue.text: Spoof act I find fault with, therefore

indicators.note: finding fault with something means pulling it apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic slates a parody routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipso facto is Latin for by that very fact, used to mean therefore.

clue.text: Offloaded peacekeepers and hurried to get "with it"

parts.note: UN is the United Nations, which provides peacekeepers

indicators.note: to get says the hurried word takes in the with-it word

parts.note: sped means hurried
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: Troops were unloaded and rushed to look fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To unship cargo is to take it off a vessel, so unshipped means offloaded.

clue.text: D made it black on both sides

indicators.note: on means the black letter is placed before the next piece

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ambi- is the prefix meaning both sides, as in ambidextrous

explanation.surface: Disney made something black all over.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is Disney's 1942 film about a young deer.

clue.text: Rose had compulsion to enter empty outhouse

indicators.note: to enter puts the compulsion inside the emptied outhouse
empty says the middle letters of the outhouse word are removed

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
the two middle letters of the outhouse word, taken out to leave it empty
a compulsion is an urge, here something the subject had

explanation.surface: Rose felt a sudden need to go into the empty shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name; it is the past tense of rise. 'empty' cuts SHED to its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Surged means rose suddenly and powerfully, as a wave or crowd does.

clue.text: D made the boy move around

parts.note: Peter is a boy's name, here the boy who never grew up
to pan is to swing a camera around a scene

explanation.surface: Disney made the boy relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is Disney's 1953 animated film of J M Barrie's play.
